purpose: Teach: 旦那/友だち/僕たち/中華/居酒屋/あいさつ/さっそく/金曜日

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、ご近所の、本気で、絶対、旦那、絶対、さん、絶対、お祖父ちゃんと、絶対、よく、絶対、お話、絶対、するわよな、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: You remember how Grandpa used to talk with our neighbor's husband all the time?
lines.style: Soft, nostalgic opening. Gentle pull backward in time. Voice has the texture of someone visiting a memory they're not sure they should disturb. Quiet conviction underneath — testing if she remembers too.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん。若い頃の、本気で、絶対、お祖父ちゃんの、絶対、友だち、絶対、皆、絶対、お元気かしらね、あなた
lines.en: Yes. I wonder how all of Grandpa's friends from back then are doing now.
lines.style: Warm agreement, but the wondering cracks it open. Slow pace on the names and the wondering — she's genuinely turning it over. Soft trailing-off, like she's actually curious and a little sad at the same time.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、僕たち、絶対、家族、絶対、お祖父ちゃん、絶対、誇りに思ったぞ、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: Back then, we were all so proud of Grandpa. You remember that?
lines.style: Quieter now, more direct. The pride sits heavy in the voice — not boasting, but remembering something real. Slight pause before 'remember' — giving her space to land on it herself.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、中華、絶対、料理屋、絶対、お祖父ちゃんと、絶対、行ったわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: Oh yes — we went to that Chinese place with Grandpa, didn't we? I remember that.
lines.style: Brightness surfaces for a moment — a specific memory lighting up. Quick, warm, then settling back into the gentler register. The word 'remember' carries the weight of certainty.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、駅前の、絶対、居酒屋、絶対、お父さん、絶対、お祝い、絶対、したわよな、ばあさん、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: And that celebration at the izakaya near the station for Father's promotion — you remember, Gran?
lines.style: Steady, clear recollection. The details anchor him. Voice rises slightly with the pride of the memory, then softens when he checks in with her — not demanding, but inviting her to confirm what he's holding.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お祖父ちゃん、絶対、ご近所への、絶対、あいさつ、絶対、丁寧でしたわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: Grandpa was always so polite when greeting the neighbors. Don't you remember that about him?
lines.style: Soft assertion — she's not asking, she's remembering out loud and inviting agreement. Slow, deliberate pace on 'polite' — it meant something. Trailing warmth at the end, gratitude in the remembering.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、さっそく、絶対、お父さん、絶対、新しい商売、絶対、始めたぞ、ばあさん、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: And then Father started that new business right away — you remember how quickly things moved, Gran?
lines.style: Quickens slightly on 'right away' — capturing the momentum of that time. Then settles into the question with genuine curiosity. Not reciting, but actually asking her to help him hold the timeline together.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、金曜日、絶対、お祖父ちゃん、絶対、お給料日、絶対、嬉しそうだったわよ、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: Grandpa was so happy on payday Fridays back then. I can still see how pleased he looked.
lines.style: Gentle smile in the voice — the pleasure is real and remembered with affection. Slow pace, savoring the small joy. Trails off softly on the image of his pleasure, like she's watching it again.
